claims.text: An optimal Al concentration exists in lightweight Al–Ti–V–Cr–Mn high-entropy alloys.
The optimal Al concentration is approximately 10 at.%.
An optimal Al concentration thermodynamically favors formation of a coherent alumina passivating scale.
The alumina passivating scale is self-healing.
The high-entropy matrix stabilizes the alumina scale.
The alumina scale retards high-temperature oxidation.
The alumina scale improves corrosion resistance in room-temperature saline environments.
The high-entropy matrix maintains mechanical strength while the protective oxide forms.
The proposed alloy design maintains low density while providing strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance.
Al concentrations below the optimum produce an insufficient or discontinuous protective oxide scale.
Al concentrations above the optimum promote brittle intermetallic phases.
The brittle intermetallic phases formed at excessive Al concentrations undermine mechanical integrity.
A composition near 10 at.% Al will outperform variants near 5 and 15 at.% Al in oxidation resistance, corrosion resistance, and retention of mechanical strength.
The proposed mechanism will cease to operate at temperatures significantly below 800°C because oxide-formation kinetics will not be activated.
The proposed mechanism will cease to hold at temperatures that destabilize the alloy phases or cause scale delamination or uncontrolled intermetallic formation.
